eventMetadata.context_description:
**The near-certain market pricing on 31°C reflects direct observational confirmation from the Hong Kong Observatory (HKO) that the absolute daily maximum temperature on August 15, 2026, reached exactly 31°C at the reference headquarters station in Tsim Sha Tsui.**

Following the record heat episode on August 9 (36.9°C at HKO headquarters under the influence of Tropical Cyclone Dolphin), a moderating southwesterly flow and partly cloudy conditions with isolated showers and thunderstorms returned typical mid-August climatology. HKO forecasts consistently projected a 28–33°C range, and real-time regional station data aligned with a daytime peak of 31°C, consistent with post-heatwave stabilization and normal seasonal variability around the long-term August mean of roughly 31–32°C.

The 99.9% implied probability on 31°C represents aggregated trader consensus on finalized HKO data (the “Absolute Daily Max” value that will resolve the market). Only an unforeseen revision in the official daily extract or an anomalous station discrepancy could shift resolution, both of which are highly improbable given the completed observational record.

eventMetadata.context_description: Under a persistent high-pressure dome over the Southeast, National Weather Service forecasts for Atlanta on August 16 center on a maximum near 95°F amid mostly sunny skies, light winds, and only a slight afternoon thunderstorm risk that limits evaporative cooling. This setup favors strong daytime heating consistent with mid-August climatology, where seasonal norms reach the low 90s but heat waves can push readings 3–5°F higher via subsidence warming and elevated dew points. Recent model runs and heat advisories through the evening underscore these conditions, with traders assigning 60% implied probability to the 96–97°F bin and 15% to 98–99°F as they weigh potential model biases toward under-forecasting peak insolation. Updated NWS briefings and next model cycle remain key near-term catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official National Weather Service forecasts for Austin on August 16 point to a high near 101°F under mostly sunny conditions with south-southwest flow, aligning closely with the market’s leading 56.5% implied probability for the 100-101°F bin. Model consensus shows limited potential for slight intensification to 102-103°F but low odds of exceeding 103°F given current steering patterns and historical August peaks rarely surpassing 102°F without stronger synoptic support. Traders are weighting these NWS and private model runs heavily ahead of official Austin-Bergstrom observations at day’s end.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Market-implied odds favor 26°C as Mexico City’s daily maximum on August 16, reflecting the latest model consensus from agencies such as the Servicio Meteorológico Nacional and international guidance showing afternoon highs near 25–26 °C under partly cloudy skies with scattered showers.**  

At 2,240 m elevation, the city’s highland location caps typical August maxima around the long-term 24 °C average, yet reduced cloud cover or delayed precipitation timing in recent model runs has nudged probabilities toward the upper end of the normal range. Traders are weighting the narrow spread between 25 °C and 27 °C outcomes because small shifts in boundary-layer moisture or solar insolation—common during the peak of the rainy season—can alter the peak by 1–2 °C. Upcoming afternoon observations and updated short-range forecasts will determine whether the realized high settles at the market’s leading 26 °C bin or shifts lower with earlier convective development.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Recent monsoon activity and official forecasts are the main drivers of trader sentiment for Lucknow's August 17 maximum temperature.** The India Meteorological Department (IMD) projects a high of 29°C under overcast skies with spells of rain or thundershowers and a heavy rainfall warning, which aligns with the near-even market split between 29°C and 30°C (both ~29.5% implied probability). Widespread cloud cover reduces incoming solar radiation while evaporative cooling from precipitation limits daytime warming, keeping temperatures below typical late-monsoon averages of 31–33°C. Minor differences among numerical weather models on rainfall timing and intensity create the tight contest between these two outcomes, with lower probabilities assigned to 31°C or higher due to expected suppression from active convection. Updated IMD briefings and model runs in the next 24 hours will likely resolve remaining uncertainty before market close.

**Official forecasts from Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration (CWA) currently project a daytime high of 35–36 °C for Taipei on August 17, aligning closely with the market’s leading outcomes at 35 °C (40.5 %) and 36 °C (27 %).**

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Kuala Lumpur Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 17 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Kuala Lumpur Intl Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/my/sepang-district/WMKK.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus clusters tightly around 33–34°C for Kuala Lumpur’s daily maximum on August 17 because official forecasts from sources such as timeanddate and the UK Met Office project highs of 33–34°C under prevailing equatorial conditions. Afternoon thunderstorm timing and cloud cover remain the key variables that could shift the peak by 1°C: early or widespread convection tends to suppress the maximum, while clearer skies and stronger solar insolation push readings toward the upper end of the range. Historical August data show typical maxima of 32–33°C with occasional spikes to 35°C driven by urban heat retention and high humidity, and current model consensus places tomorrow near this baseline without strong signals for extreme deviation. The narrow spread between the leading outcomes reflects genuine uncertainty in short-term convective development rather than divergent long-term trends.
